title: Inkább... Mint...: Preferring One Option, Gently

sections.title: Naming a preference without deciding for anyone
sections.content: You know *inkább ... mint ...* from A2 (Unit 29: *Inkább teát iszom, mint kávét*). Use it with a conditional verb and you get a soft, personal preference rather than a decision handed down: *Én inkább X-et választanám, mint Y-t* states what you would pick, leaving the real choice with the listener — the same gentle register as *-hat/-het* suggestions in Lesson 2.

items.spanish: Én inkább a biztonságos utat választanám, mint a gyorsabbat.
items.english: I would rather choose the safe route than the faster one.

items.spanish: A te helyedben inkább várnék egy kicsit, mint azonnal döntenék.
items.english: In your place, I'd rather wait a bit than decide right away.

items.spanish: Inkább most beszélnél vele, mint később?
items.english: Would you rather talk to him/her now than later?

sections.content: *mint* introduces the option being passed over: either a short phrase (*mint a gyorsabbat*) or a second conditional verb (*mint azonnal döntenék*). Either way you don't repeat the subject after *mint*.
